title: Old records and how stereo would have served Oliver's band
summary: He says early recording failed to capture the drums and bass, and Oliver's band would be a sensation on modern equipment.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: Well, I just happened to be on the ground floor and I heard them all in person through a lot of records. A lot of records I hear, and those days they weren't so particular about recording jazz bands and recording managers. They'd just turn on the machine and just go ahead and play. And if they had some of those bands today, with the stereo equipment and all that, if Joe Oliver had that band today, the band he had that I heard, it would be a sensation right today.
It would. If they were recorded on stereo, when I heard them, it would be really fun. It wouldn't sound carny or anything about it today, even if they played just the same
way. That's right. They'd still be modern, huh?

Because a lot of people hear some of those records and they say, oh, that sounds awful. Yeah. Well, it does to me too, on account of the recordings. Yeah. But if they had that good equipment like they have today, it wouldn't sound.
Because it couldn't pick up the drums or anything. None of the bass came through. No, it couldn't pick up the bass at all.
